**XEarthLayer 0.5.0** brings macOS support, night lighting, a rebuilt scenery world and a package manager.

**If you are upgrading from 0.4.x, read [Upgrading from 0.4.x](#upgrading-from-04x) before you install any scenery.** The rebuilt world replaces the old one, and the two must not be installed together.

| Platform | Download |
|---|---|
| Debian, Ubuntu (glibc 2.34 or newer) | `xearthlayer_0.5.0-1_amd64.deb` |
| Fedora 44 or newer | `xearthlayer-0.5.0-1.fc44.x86_64.rpm` |
| Arch and derivatives | `aur-package.zip` (`PKGBUILD` and `.SRCINFO`; unpack it and run `makepkg -si`) |
| Other Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.34 or newer) | `xearthlayer-v0.5.0-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` |
| macOS, Apple Silicon | `xearthlayer-v0.5.0-arm64-macos.pkg`, Homebrew (below), or `xearthlayer-v0.5.0-arm64-macos.tar.gz` |

There is no Intel Mac build. The `xearthlayer-publish` downloads are the tool for building scenery packages, which you only need if you publish your own.

---

## What is new

**macOS.** XEarthLayer now runs natively on Apple Silicon, with X-Plane and scenery working as they do on Linux. Every build is signed and notarized by Apple. Thanks to [@dlicudi](https://github.com/dlicudi) for leading the port.

**Night lighting.** Ortho scenery used to leave cities dark at night wherever autogen lights did not reach. XEarthLayer now generates lit textures on your machine, from a night recipe in each package, NASA's measurements of how bright the ground really is, and the lit art in your own X-Plane installation. Some neighbourhoods are lit with white LED street lighting rather than sodium orange, at a share and colour temperature set by region. It is on by default; see `night.enabled` and `night.brightness` in the [configuration reference](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/blob/main/docs/configuration.md).

**A rebuilt world.** The scenery library is now 17 regions built from scratch with night recipes, about 161 GB if you install the whole planet. Package archives are smaller too, because DSF files are now compressed the way Laminar compresses its own scenery.

**A package manager.** `xearthlayer packages` opens a full-screen manager with Local, Library, Progress and Settings tabs. Downloads no longer wait for installs, so a batch takes about as long as its downloads. Region codes can be shortened: `xearthlayer packages install na-canada eu-west` installs every package beneath those codes. Ctrl+C cancels cleanly, and a package being replaced keeps its old version.

**SimHeaven X-World Pro.** With `packages.xworld_pro` on, XEarthLayer detects which continents X-World Pro covers, leaves out its own overlays there, and checks your `scenery_packs.ini` order on every start. It advises only and never edits the file. See [x-world-pro.md](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/blob/main/docs/x-world-pro.md).

**X-Plane comes first.** Prefetch now runs in its own lane with its own workers and download connections, so a backlog of prefetch work can no longer sit in front of a tile X-Plane is waiting for. While X-Plane is waiting on a tile to be generated, prefetch starts nothing new. A timed-out job now stops downloading at once and gives back its capacity, which used to leak away over a session.

**A faster start.** `run` no longer sizes every installed package before the dashboard opens, and after a package change the scenery index rebuilds in about 17 seconds rather than over four minutes with the whole world installed.

**A better dashboard.** A Status pane shows X-Plane's frame rate and what is actually running this session: the texture encoder, night lighting and X-World Pro. The prefetch section shows one clear state and how much of its capacity is in use, and the Scenery System section shows how long X-Plane waited for tiles.

The [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has the full list.

---

## Install

Close X-Plane and stop any running XEarthLayer first.

**Debian and Ubuntu:** `sudo apt install ./xearthlayer_0.5.0-1_amd64.deb`

**Fedora:** `sudo dnf install ./xearthlayer-0.5.0-1.fc44.x86_64.rpm`

**Other Linux, from the tarball:**

```bash
tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.0-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
```

**macOS:** XEarthLayer needs [macFUSE](https://macfuse.io), including its one-time approval. The [macOS guide](https://xearthlayer.app/docs/macos/) walks through it. Then choose one:

- **Installer package.** Open `xearthlayer-v0.5.0-arm64-macos.pkg` and follow the Installer. It puts `xearthlayer` in `/usr/local/bin`, and installs without a network connection.
- **Homebrew.** `brew install --cask xearthlayer/tap/xearthlayer`. If macFUSE is already installed from its own installer, add `--skip-cask-deps`.
- **Tarball.** Unpack it and move `xearthlayer` to `~/.local/bin`. The first run needs a network connection, because macOS checks the notarization once.

**Then check it:** `xearthlayer --version` should print `0.5.0`.

**New to XEarthLayer?** Run `xearthlayer setup`. When it finishes it offers to open the package manager, where you install the regions you fly (below).

---

## Upgrading from 0.4.x

The first command you run copies your `config.ini` to the platform's standard location (`~/.config/xearthlayer/` on Linux) and may ask you to confirm. Accepting is safe: nothing else is moved, and the old `config.ini` is kept, so 0.4.x still works if you go back to it. The copy reads the rebuilt library, and the message says so; the old file keeps the library 0.4.x can use. Then:

```bash
xearthlayer config upgrade
```

**Remove every old package before installing anything new:**

```bash
xearthlayer packages remove --all --force
xearthlayer packages remove --all --type overlay --force
xearthlayer packages list    # should report no packages installed
```

If you had no overlays, the second line prints `Error: Package manager error: No overlay packages are installed`, which is harmless. There is nothing to clean up by hand in `Custom Scenery`.

Two other changes to know about:

- `xearthlayer publish` is now its own program, `xearthlayer-publish`, with the same subcommands, in its own package.
- `prefetch.mode` is gone: prefetch is on or off by `prefetch.enabled`. A configuration that switched prefetch off still has it off, and `xearthlayer config upgrade` tidies it up.

**Coming from a 0.5.0 alpha, beta or rc?** Install this build; your packages carry over. On Homebrew, leave the pre-release channel first with `brew uninstall --cask xearthlayer@prerelease`. From an alpha, also run `xearthlayer config upgrade`.

## Install the regions you fly

```bash
xearthlayer packages
```

Press `2` for the Library, move with the arrow keys, mark regions with `Space`, press `i` and confirm with `y`. Press `3` to watch the downloads and installs. `?` lists every key, and `q` quits. To have each ortho install bring its region's overlays, which is off by default, set `packages.auto_install_overlays` on the Settings tab.

| Region | Covers | Download |
|---|---|---|
| `NA-USA-BERMUDA-BAHAMAS` | Contiguous US, Alaska, Hawaii, Bermuda, the Bahamas, Turks and Caicos | 14.1 GB |
| `NA-MEXICO-CENTRAL` | Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean | 4.5 GB |
| `NA-CANADA-WEST` | Canada west of 95° W | 10.2 GB |
| `NA-CANADA-EAST` | Canada east of 95° W | 13.2 GB |
| `NA-GREENLAND` | Greenland | 0.8 GB |
| `SA-WEST` | Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, the Guianas | 9.2 GB |
| `SA-EAST` | Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay, the Falklands | 8.8 GB |
| `EU-WEST` | Europe west of Russia, Iceland, Scandinavia, the Mediterranean | 16.1 GB |
| `EU-EAST` | European Russia west of the Urals | 3.7 GB |
| `AF-NORTH` | North and West Africa | 7.3 GB |
| `AF-SOUTH` | Central, East and Southern Africa | 9.1 GB |
| `AS-INDIA-MIDDLE-EAST-HIMALAYAN` | Middle East, Central Asia, the Indian subcontinent | 16.8 GB |
| `AS-CHINA-MONGOLIA` | China and Mongolia | 18.5 GB |
| `AS-ASIA-PACIFIC` | Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Southeast Asia, the Philippines | 11.6 GB |
| `AS-RUSSIA-CENTRAL` | Siberia from the Urals to Lake Baikal | 4.8 GB |
| `AS-RUSSIA-EAST` | The Russian Far East | 6.4 GB |
| `OC-AUSTRALIA-NZ-PACIFIC` | Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific islands | 5.5 GB |

Sizes are download sizes. Then start streaming:

```bash
xearthlayer run
```

---

## Known issues

**FUSE read counts on the dashboard are low on macOS.** macOS serves repeat reads of a texture from its own cache, so XEarthLayer only sees the first one. Nothing else depends on that count.

**Saving a setting rewrites `config.ini` from its template.** Comments you added to the file by hand are lost. The values are kept.

**Antarctica is not in the library yet.**
